relevance_reason: Reports RAPSN N88K mutation in 12 CMS patients from 10 European families with AChR deficiency-associated CMS, with clinical description and founder effect.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2003) screened 120 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome from 110 unrelated families for the RAPSN N88K mutation by restriction fragment length polymorphism and sequence analysis, and identified N88K in 12 patients from 10 independent families, either in homozygous state or in compound heterozygous state with another missense mutation.
quotes: One hundred twenty CMS patients from 110 unrelated families were analyzed for the RAPSN mutation N88K by restriction fragment length polymorphism and sequence analysis.
In 12 CMS patients from 10 independent families, RAPSN N88K was identified either homozygous or heteroallelic to another missense mutation.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2003) reported that in 12 CMS patients with RAPSN N88K, symptoms usually began perinatally or in the first years of life, although 1 patient had no myasthenic symptoms before the third decade. Typical features included bilateral ptosis, weakness of facial, bulbar, and limb muscles, and frequent crisis-like exacerbations with respiratory insufficiency provoked by stress, fever, or infections in early childhood. Patients generally had mild to moderate myasthenic symptoms, but severity and onset varied greatly.
quotes: Symptoms usually started perinatally or in the first years of life. However, one patient did not show any myasthenic symptoms before the third decade.
Clinical symptoms typically included bilateral ptosis, weakness of facial, bulbar, and limb muscles, and a favorable response to anticholinesterase treatment.
Crisis-like exacerbations with respiratory insufficiency provoked by stress, fever, or infections in early childhood were frequent.

phenotypes.text: onset perinatally or in first years of life

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2003) found that patients with RAPSN N88K showed a favorable response to anticholinesterase treatment.
quotes: In general, patients (RAPSN N88K) were characterized by mild to moderate myasthenic symptoms with favorable response to anticholinesterase treatment.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2003) found that all RAPSN N88K families originated from Central or Western European countries, and genotype analysis indicated derivation from a common founder; they concluded that N88K is a frequent cause of rapsyn-related CMS in European patients.
quotes: All RAPSN N88K families originate from Central or Western European countries. Genotype analysis indicated that they derive from a common ancestor (founder).
The RAPSN mutation N88K is a frequent cause of rapsyn-related CMS in European patients.

relevance_reason: Reports patients with CMS who carry RAPSN mutations, including N88K and three other variants, with genotype-severity observations.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2003) described 4 patients from 4 unrelated families with congenital myasthenic syndrome and RAPSN mutations. In 2 cases the diagnosis was confirmed by microelectrode and electron microscopy studies. The patient homozygous for N88K was only mildly affected, and the 3 compound heterozygous patients were severely affected.
quotes: We have identified four patients from four different families with RAPSNmutations and CMS, confirmed in two cases by microelectrode and electron microscopy studies.

One patient who was homozygous for N88K was only mildly affected, while the other three patients who were heterozygous for N88K and a second mutation (either L14P, 46insC, or Y269X) were severely affected.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2003) found the RAPSN N88K mutation in all 4 patients with CMS from 4 families: 1 patient was homozygous and 3 were compound heterozygous with a second RAPSN mutation. N88K lies within the putative leucine zipper motif, which may be important for AChR clustering.
quotes: The N88K mutation was present in all patients.
N88K occurs within the putative leucine zipper motif potentially important for AChR clustering.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2003) found a RAPSN L14P mutation together with N88K in a severely affected compound heterozygous patient with CMS. The authors predicted that L14P causes a conformational change at the N terminus that may disrupt membrane association.
quotes: L14P predicts a conformational change at the N-terminus that may disrupt membrane association.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2003) found a RAPSN 46insC mutation together with N88K in a severely affected compound heterozygous patient with CMS. The authors predicted that 46insC truncates the protein.
quotes: Mutations 46insC and Y269X predicts truncation of the protein.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2003) found a RAPSN Y269X nonsense mutation together with N88K in a severely affected compound heterozygous patient with CMS. The authors predicted that Y269X truncates the protein.
quotes: Mutations 46insC and Y269X predicts truncation of the protein.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2003) observed that the patient homozygous for the RAPSN N88K mutation was mildly affected. The 3 compound heterozygous patients, who carried N88K with L14P, 46insC, or Y269X, were severely affected. The authors suggested that the predicted effects of these second mutations may explain the severe disease in the compound heterozygotes.
quotes: One patient who was homozygous for N88K was only mildly affected, while the other three patients who were heterozygous for N88K and a second mutation (either L14P, 46insC, or Y269X) were severely affected.
These findings may explain the severe clinical involvement of compound heterozygous patients.

relevance_reason: Reports a CMS patient with AChR deficiency-type RAPSN compound heterozygosity (N88K plus a novel ~4.5-kb deletion).

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2004) described a German patient with sporadic congenital myasthenic syndrome of early onset associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, recurrent episodes of respiratory insufficiency provoked by infections, and moderate general weakness responsive to anticholinesterase treatment.
quotes: Clinically, the patient presents with an early onset CMS, associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, recurrent episodes of respiratory insufficiency provoked by infections, and a moderate general weakness, responsive to anticholinesterase treatment.

phenotypes.text: recurrent episodes of respiratory insufficiency provoked by infections

findings.statement: In a sporadic German patient with CMS, Müller et al. (2004) used RFLP, long-range PCR and sequence analysis to identify compound heterozygosity for the RAPSN N88K mutation and a large deletion of about 4.5 kb disrupting the RAPSN gene.
quotes: A sporadic CMS patient from Germany was analyzed for RAPSN mutations by RFLP, long-range PCR and sequence analysis.
The mutation RAPSN N88K was found heterozygously to a large deletion of about 4.5 kb disrupting the RAPSN gene.

variants.as_reported: large deletion of about 4.5 kb disrupting the RAPSN gene

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2004) suggested that the RAPSN 4.5-kb deletion may have been caused by Alu-mediated unequal homologous recombination and hypothesized that numerous interspersed Alu elements may predispose the RAPSN locus to genetic rearrangements.
quotes: Interestingly, an Alu-mediated unequal homologous recombination may have caused the deletion.
We hypothesize that numerous interspersed Alu elements may predispose the RAPSN locus for genetic rearrangements.

relevance_reason: Reports RAPSN promoter E-box mutations in 8 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome, plus functional studies predicting endplate AChR deficiency.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -27C-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter region in a patient with congenital myasthenic syndrome (patient 1). The mutation changes an E-box at -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG, and the allele harboring it was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. Position +1 was the major transcriptional start site, determined to be 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site.
quotes: Patient 1 carries -27C-->G that changes an E-box at -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. An allele harboring -27C-->G is not transcribed in patient's muscle.
For each mutation, position +1 represents the major transcriptional start site that we determine to be 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -38A-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter region in 7 patients (patients 2-8) with congenital myasthenic syndrome, all of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin. The mutation changes an E-box at -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG, which does not affect the consensus CANNTG sequence.
quotes: Patients 2-8 are of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations, and harbor -38A-->G that changes another E-box at -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG, which does not affect the consensus CANNTG sequence.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) reported that the 7 congenital myasthenic syndrome patients of Oriental Jewish Iraqi or Iranian origin carrying the RAPSN -38A-G promoter mutation had facial malformations.
quotes: Patients 2-8 are of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) showed by haplotype analysis that the RAPSN -38A-G promoter mutation in Oriental Jewish patients of Iraqi or Iranian origin arose from a common founder.
quotes: Haplotype analysis shows that -38A-->G arises from a common founder.

findings.statement: In electrophoretic mobility shift assays, Ohno et al. (2003) found that the RAPSN -38A-G mutation gained, and -27C-G lost, binding affinity for different components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts. In luciferase reporter assays, both mutations attenuated reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes. The -27C-G mutation also attenuated expression in HEK cells transfected with MyoD or myogenin, and it markedly attenuated the enhancer activity of an E-box on an SV40 promoter. The authors concluded that impaired RAPSN promoter activity predicts reduced rapsyn expression and endplate acetylcholine receptor deficiency.
quotes: Electrophoretic mobility shift assays reveal that -38A-->G gains, and -27C-->G looses, binding affinity for different components of nuclear extracts of C2C12 myotubes.

Luciferase reporter assays show that both -38A-->G and -27C-->G attenuate reporter gene expression in C2C12 myotubes, and that -27C-->G additionally attenuates reporter gene expression in MyoD- or myogenin-transfected HEK cells.
Impaired transcriptional activities of the RAPSN promoter region predict reduced rapsyn expression and endplate acetylcholine receptor deficiency.

relevance_reason: Reports RAPSN mutations, including the common N88K allele, in 16 unrelated patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome, and describes early- and late-onset phenotypes.

findings.statement: Burke et al. (2003) identified rapsyn (RAPSN) mutations in 16 unrelated patients with congenital/hereditary myasthenic syndrome. All 16 patients carried the N88K mutation.
quotes: Rapsyn mutations in 16 unrelated patients with a congenital/hereditary myasthenic syndrome were identified, and a mutation (N88K) common to each of them was found.

findings.statement: Burke et al. (2003) described two distinct phenotypes among 16 patients with RAPSN-related congenital myasthenic syndrome: early onset and late onset. The early-onset form was often associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises. The late-onset form developed in adolescence or adulthood and was at first mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.
quotes: Two distinct phenotypes were noted: early and late onset. The former is frequently associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises.
The late-onset phenotype developed in adolescence or adulthood and was initially mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.

phenotypes.text: myasthenia with onset in adolescence or adulthood

findings.statement: Burke et al. (2003) noted that the late-onset RAPSN phenotype can be mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis, and that recognizing it should prevent inappropriate immunotherapy.
quotes: Recognition of this late-onset phenotype should prevent inappropriate immunotherapy.

relevance_reason: This paper first identifies recessive RAPSN mutations in patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome and endplate AChR deficiency.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) identified 3 recessive rapsyn (RAPSN) mutations in 4 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome and endplate AChR deficiency who had no mutations in AChR-subunit genes. One patient carried L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3, 2 were homozygous for N88K, and 1 carried N88K and 553ins5, a frameshift in TPR5.
quotes: In four patients with EP AChR deficiency but with no mutations in AChR subunits, we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; two are homozygous for N88K; and one carries N88K and 553ins5, which frameshifts in TPR5.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) found an L14P missense mutation in tetratricopeptide repeat 1 (TPR1) of rapsyn (RAPSN). It was in the compound heterozygous state with N88K in a patient with congenital myasthenic syndrome and endplate AChR deficiency.
quotes: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) found a 553ins5 insertion in rapsyn (RAPSN) that causes a frameshift in TPR5. It was in the compound heterozygous state with N88K in a patient with congenital myasthenic syndrome and endplate AChR deficiency.
quotes: one carries N88K and 553ins5, which frameshifts in TPR5

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) performed endplate studies in each of the 4 patients with RAPSN mutations. These showed decreased staining for rapsyn and AChR and impaired postsynaptic morphological development.
quotes: EP studies in each case show decreased staining for rapsyn and AChR, as well as impaired postsynaptic morphological development.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) expressed the mutant rapsyn proteins in HEK cells. None of the 3 mutations hindered rapsyn self-association, but all 3 reduced coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.
quotes: Expression studies in HEK cells indicate that none of the mutations hinders rapsyn self-association but that all three diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with CMS and AChR deficiency who was homozygous for the RAPSN N88K mutation, with morphological and electrophysiological characterization.

findings.statement: Yasaki et al. (2004) reported a 28-year-old French man with congenital myasthenic syndrome who had had mild diplopia and fatigability since age 5 years. His muscle biopsy showed a marked reduction in rapsyn and acetylcholine receptor (AChR) at neuromuscular junctions, as well as a simplified subneural apparatus.
quotes: Here, we report the case of a 28-year-old French congenital myasthenic syndrome patient who had mild diplopia and fatigability from the age of 5 years.
His muscle biopsy revealed a marked reduction in rapsyn and acetylcholine receptor at neuromuscular junctions together with a simplification of the subneural apparatus structure.

phenotypes.text: reduced acetylcholine receptor at neuromuscular junctions
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction

findings.statement: In a French patient with congenital myasthenic syndrome and AChR deficiency, Yasaki et al. (2004) ruled out mutations in the AChR subunit genes and found a homozygous N88K mutation in the RAPSN gene. Cell expression studies had previously shown that this mutation impairs aggregation of rapsyn and AChR at the neuromuscular junction.
quotes: In this patient, we excluded mutations in the acetylcholine receptor subunit genes and identified the homozygous N88K rapsyn mutation, which has already been shown by cell expression to impair rapsyn and acetylcholine receptor aggregation at the neuromuscular junction.

findings.statement: Yasaki et al. (2004) found the RAPSN N88K mutation in the heterozygous state in 5 of 300 unrelated control subjects. They concluded that the mutation is not infrequent in the healthy population.
quotes: The detection of the N88K mutation at the heterozygous state in five of 300 unrelated control subjects shows that this mutation is not infrequent in the healthy population.

findings.statement: Yasaki et al. (2004) performed electrophysiological studies on biopsied intercostal muscle from a patient homozygous for the RAPSN N88K mutation. They found that the fatigable weakness reflected both reduced AChR density in the membrane and a decline in endplate potentials evoked at low frequency.
quotes: Electrophysiological measurements on biopsied intercostal muscle from this patient showed that his rapsyn mutation-induced fatigable weakness is expressed not only in a diminution in acetylcholine receptor membrane density but also in a decline of endplate potentials evoked at low frequency.

phenotypes.text: decline of endplate potentials at low-frequency stimulation
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction

relevance_reason: Large case series of patients with rapsyn-deficient congenital myasthenic syndrome, with clinical, endplate and molecular findings.

findings.statement: Milone et al. (2009) reported clinical, electrophysiologic, pathologic, and molecular studies in 39 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome due to rapsyn defects. In all but 1 patient, the disease presented in the first 2 years of life. Nine patients had constant or episodic ophthalmoparesis, 1 patient had a pure limb-girdle phenotype, and more than half had intermittent exacerbations.
quotes: Clinical, electrophysiologic, pathologic, and molecular studies were done in 39 patients.

In all but one patient, the disease presented in the first 2 years of life. In 9 patients, the myasthenic symptoms included constant or episodic ophthalmoparesis, and 1 patient had a pure limb-girdle phenotype.
More than one-half of the patients experienced intermittent exacerbations.

phenotypes.text: onset in first 2 years of life

findings.statement: Milone et al. (2009) had long-term follow-up for 25 patients after the start of cholinergic therapy: 21 became stable or improved (2 becoming asymptomatic), 3 had a progressive course, and 1 died in infancy. The authors concluded that with early diagnosis and therapy, rapsyn deficiency has a benign course in most patients.
quotes: Long-term follow-up was available in 25 patients after start of cholinergic therapy: 21 became stable or were improved and 2 of these became asymptomatic; 3 had a progressive course; and 1 died in infancy.
With early diagnosis and therapy, rapsyn deficiency has a benign course in most patients.

findings.statement: Milone et al. (2009) found in 7 patients who had endplate studies that the average AChR count per endplate and the synaptic response to ACh were less reduced than in patients with low-expressor AChR mutations.
quotes: In 7 patients who had endplate studies, the average counts of AChR per endplate and the synaptic response to ACh were less reduced than in patients harboring low AChR expressor mutations.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction

findings.statement: Among 39 patients with rapsyn-deficient congenital myasthenic syndrome, Milone et al. (2009) found that 8 were homozygous and 23 heterozygous for the common N88K mutation in the RAPSN gene. Homozygosity for N88K was associated with varying grades of severity.
quotes: Eight patients were homozygous and 23 heterozygous for the common p.N88K mutation.
Homozygosity for p.N88K was associated with varying grades of severity.

findings.statement: Milone et al. (2009) identified 6 novel RAPSN mutations in their cohort, comprising 3 missense mutations, an in-frame deletion, a splice-site mutation, and a nonsense mutation.
quotes: Six mutations, comprising 3 missense mutations, an in-frame deletion, a splice-site mutation, and a nonsense mutation, are novel.

findings.statement: Milone et al. (2009) observed no genotype-phenotype correlations except in 8 Near-Eastern patients homozygous for the RAPSN promoter E-box mutation c.-38A>G, who had a mild course; this E-box mutation was associated with jaw deformities.
quotes: No genotype-phenotype correlations were observed except in 8 Near-Eastern patients homozygous for the promoter mutation (c.-38A>G), who had a mild course.
There was no consistent phenotype-genotype correlation except for an E-box mutation associated with jaw deformities.

relevance_reason: Haplotype analysis of the RAPSN N88K mutation supporting a founder effect in CMS associated with AChR deficiency; also notes asymptomatic homozygotes.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2004) used 7 intragenic SNPs spanning 8 kb of the RAPSN gene to characterize the haplotype associated with the N88K mutation. In 3 affected N88K homozygotes, they identified a common haplotype that was present in all heterozygous carriers of N88K, supporting a founder effect.
quotes: we used seven intragenic single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) spanning 8 kb to characterize the haplotype associated with N88K
In three affected N88K homozygous individuals, we identified a common haplotype present in all heterozygous carriers of N88K.
Our findings of a common haplotype associated with the N88K mutation support a founder effect.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2004) found that 2 asymptomatic individuals homozygous for the RAPSN N88K mutation carried a second haplotype that differed at 3 SNP sites downstream of the mutation. The authors suggested that recombination events may have occurred within the rapsyn gene and that this may have implications for phenotypic expression of the disease.
quotes: Of note, in two asymptomatic N88K homozygous individuals, a second haplotype was present that differed at three SNP sites downstream from the N88K mutation.

The discordant haplotype found in homozygous individuals suggests that recombination events may have occurred within the rapsyn gene and that this may have implications in the phenotypic expression of the disease.

relevance_reason: The title reports a congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by two RAPSN mutations that are not N88K, which is directly about CMS11. Only the title was available, so the details cannot be extracted.

findings.statement: Maselli et al. (2007) reported congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by two rapsyn (RAPSN) mutations other than N88K.
quotes: Congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by two non-N88K rapsyn mutations.

relevance_reason: The title reports RAPSN mutations, including N88K and novel variants, in congenital myasthenic syndromes. These are directly relevant to CMS11. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Richard et al. (2003) suggested a possible founder effect for the rapsyn (RAPSN) N88K mutation in patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome.
quotes: Possible founder effect of rapsyn N88K mutation and identification of novel rapsyn mutations in congenital myasthenic syndromes.

findings.statement: Richard et al. (2003) identified novel rapsyn (RAPSN) mutations in patients with congenital myasthenic syndromes.
quotes: Possible founder effect of rapsyn N88K mutation and identification of novel rapsyn mutations in congenital myasthenic syndromes.

relevance_reason: The abstract reports new recessive missense mutations in RAPSN that caused a severe but not necessarily lethal fetal akinesia phenotype. This places RAPSN-related disease on a spectrum with the congenital myasthenic syndrome, but the abstract gives no variant details.

findings.statement: Michalk et al. (2008) identified novel recessive missense mutations in RAPSN in patients with fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS) disorders. These mutations caused a severe but not necessarily lethal phenotype, whereas homozygous nonsense mutations in CHRNA1 and CHRND were lethal.
quotes: novel recessive missense mutations in RAPSN caused a severe but not necessarily lethal phenotype

findings.statement: Michalk et al. (2008) concluded that complete or severe functional disruption of fetal AChR causes lethal multiple pterygium syndrome, whereas milder alterations result in fetal hypokinesia with inborn contractures or a myasthenic syndrome later in life.
quotes: We conclude that complete or severe functional disruption of fetal AChR causes lethal multiple pterygium syndrome whereas milder alterations result in fetal hypokinesia with inborn contractures or a myasthenic syndrome later in life.

findings.statement: Michalk et al. (2008) studied Rapsn and the AChR subunit genes in mouse embryos. Expression was found in skeletal muscles and also in early somite development. The authors suggested that early developmental defects such as fetal edema, cystic hygroma, or cardiac defects might be due to somite expression, in addition to muscle-specific effects.
quotes: we studied Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrnd, Chrng, and Rapsn in mouse embryos and found expression in skeletal muscles but also in early somite development
This indicates that early developmental defects might be due to somite expression in addition to solely muscle-specific effects.
